acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

header.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the rival because it brought named people and on-call cover for on-sales. Our support tiers sounded like 'a queue with a faster timer.' Jordan thought the load test had won it.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Lead with who answers when payments fail mid on-sale.
findings.why: Payments failed four minutes into an arena on-sale, and the old provider replied only after it ended.
findings.quote: They got a reply after the on-sale was over.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Speak to the COO about a failed on-sale, not load tests.
findings.why: Halima decided alone in one meeting. Ben, the CTO, wanted us, and her only answer to his load test was 'good.'
findings.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Name the people and on-call cover behind big launch days.

line.text: Enterprise support: a technical account manager embedded in your team, with a 15-minute response for critical issues

findings.why: Ben said the rival brought its real account team and promised on-call cover. Jordan's view that this over-promised is only his guess.
findings.quote: someone on call for every major on-sale

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Replace tiers and response times with the named person who answers.

line.text: Premium support: a dedicated support manager who has ongoing context about your business

findings.why: When Halima asked who her person was, Jordan's walk through support tiers turned her against us.
findings.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Show on paper who watches and answers on on-sale morning.
findings.why: Halima asked for an on-sale plan, and we had none. Jordan also had no ticketing customer to vouch for us.
findings.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'what happens when it's down,' not uptime history.
findings.why: Halima and her team never said 'support.' They asked 'who,' and she rejected uptime as the reason to buy.
findings.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
